src: FreeREG - Northam (St Margaret) and Bideford, Devon: parish register coverage checked before searching
what: TAYLOR baptisms, Northam and Bideford, 1869-1891, for a daughter born 1882. NOTHING, AND THE NULL IS FULLY EXPLAINED RATHER THAN MERELY RECORDED. Bideford is listed as a place and has NO church, NO register and NO records at all. So this is a coverage wall, not an absent baptism, and nobody should read the zero as evidence about the family. THE SEARCH WAS RUN ANYWAY, with a control first: surname TAYLOR alone, Northam, 1869-1891, returned 0, which the contents page then explained.

src: General Register Office (gro.gov.uk) - the GRO's own online birth index for England and Wales
what: TAYLOR births with mother's maiden surname BRAYLEY, Bideford district, 1870-1893. TEN SEARCHES - five year-windows times two sexes, because sex is a mandatory field and the year range is capped at plus or minus two. NINE CHILDREN OF ONE COUPLE RECOVERED, AND A TENTH DISPROVED. THE POINT OF THIS SOURCE, which no free index can match: the GRO's own index PRINTS THE MOTHER'S MAIDEN SURNAME on every birth from 1837, so a search on father's surname plus mother's maiden name returns a couple's children BY DEFINITION rather than by inference. FreeBMD carries no mother's maiden name in its birth index and never will, which is why three weeks of candidate-weighing there could not settle what this settled in ten searches. THE CRITICAL WINDOW WAS RE-RUN ON 'SIMILAR SOUNDING VARIATIONS' because a spelling variant of the mother's surname was documented in an earlier census: 28 births across England, the same two in the district. IT NEEDS AN ACCOUNT, which the archive owner signed in; this session does not create accounts.

src: General Register Office (gro.gov.uk) - birth index, England and Wales; second pass, one generation up
what: BRAYLEY births (loose surname matching) with mother's maiden surname TEMPLE, 1838-1852, both sexes - six searches. TWO CHILDREN FOUND AND TWO ABSENCES ESTABLISHED. The method is the same as the pass before it and the lesson is sharper: searching for a PERSON who may never have been registered can only ever fail, while searching for her PARENTS returns the children who ARE in the book and therefore the shape of who is missing. THE SPELLING CONTROL IS BUILT IN - the query used one spelling of the surname and the index returned the other both times, so the absences are not an artefact. WHAT THE ABSENCES MEAN: the two earliest children, both born in a capital city in the early 1840s, are unregistered; the two later ones are registered. Birth registration was not compulsory on parents in England and Wales until the Act of 1874, in force 1875, and under-registration in the 1840s fell heaviest on the urban poor - which this household is recorded as being. Useful to anyone hunting an early-Victorian birth that will not appear.

src: FamilySearch - South Africa, Transvaal Civil Death 1869-1954 and Orange Free State Civil Death Registration 1902-1954
what: LERENA across the whole of South Africa - 413 results, every one read for an indexed PARENT. EXACTLY THREE CARRY ONE and all three are infant children of one man, none of whom appears on his own death notice because a death notice lists the living. TWO METHOD NOTES WORTH PASSING ON. (1) A DATE FILTER PRODUCED A SILENT FALSE ZERO: the same surname-plus-country query returned 0 with a date range attached and 413 without it, and nothing in the result said the filter had misfired. (2) AN AGE FIELD IN BOTH COLLECTIONS IS A DEFAULT, NOT A MEASUREMENT: two infants a decade apart are both given 'Age: 0 days', while two independent family dates give them five days and four. Two errors in the same direction is an unfilled form field. The age was discarded rather than used to correct the dates.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT SEARCH - the words on unindexed images, not an index of names
what: LERENA and the exact phrase 'Juan Carlos Lerena', tested as a ROUTE rather than worked as a search. THE POINT FOR ANY ARCHIVE: full text goes round the transcriber, so it reaches a man with a COMPOUND SURNAME who is filed under his father's name and is invisible to a search for his mother's. One such man was found in two hits across the whole corpus and correctly set aside on the surname order. WHAT THE CORPUS HOLDS FOR THE RIVER PLATE: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo MARRIAGE DISPENSATION RECORDS 1856-1932 - a class that names a groom's parents; Flores and Trinidad baptisms and deaths; Montevideo burial registers 1886-2021; Catedral baptisms and deaths. AND THE HOLE: SOUTH AFRICA IS NOT IN IT. A full-text search with a South African place filter errors outright and no South African collection surfaces unfiltered, so a Cape question gains nothing here. Recorded as a route confirmed and not yet worked.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Flores (Uruguay). Civil Birth Records 1916-1925, act No. 10 of 1922
what: The 1913 marriage dispensation of a PELAEZ groom and a LERENA bride named a degree of kinship and no parents. METHOD, AND IT IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: search the full text for the BRIDE by exact phrase, then look for a CHILD'S BIRTH ACT rather than for the marriage - because a Uruguayan civil birth act names BOTH PARENTS AND ALL FOUR GRANDPARENTS with their ages, trades and addresses. One act answered the dispensation outright and gave five adults their first recorded birth year.
note: NO WAYPOINT ESTABLISHED. A full-text image ark carries no wc=/owc= parameter, so the DGS film number is recorded instead and the waypoint is left null rather than guessed from a similar volume. Film 008165367, item 6, image 195 - read directly off the page, not inferred. CAUTION WORTH CARRYING: the AI transcript renders one clerk's single letterform as SERENA in one line and LERENA four lines later; the plate shows both are L. Read the plate before recording a surname from this corpus.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores (Uruguay). Baptism Records August 1905-August 1909

The child's baptism named the parents of both halves of the couple, merged two register rows this archive had split the same morning, and added a sixth child to a founding couple.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records, the volumes of the 1850s (1852-1855, 1855-1857, 1857-1860)
what: THE FINDING ANY ARCHIVE USING THIS COLLECTION NEEDS: it is not one record class, it is two, and the difference is the DECADE. The volumes of 1885-1913 are the Vicar General's SUMMARY LEDGER - one sentence per couple, naming no parents. The volumes of the 1850s in the SAME collection are FULL EXPEDIENTES: petition, numbered interrogatory, sworn witness depositions naming the PARENTS AND GRANDPARENTS of both parties, the Cura Vicario's report, and sometimes a KINSHIP DIAGRAM the priest drew himself. Three were read (Dec 1854, Aug 1855, Feb 1858) and all three name four generations. This archive had published twice that these records cannot name parents; both statements were generalisations from one date range.
note: NO WAYPOINT ESTABLISHED and no DGS film number is shown on these full-text pages, so both fields are left null rather than guessed; the image arks are in the url and in data/sources-consulted.tsv. HOW THEY WERE FOUND: full-text search on the exact phrase of a BRIDE's name and then a FATHER's name - 'Socorro Lerena', 'Alejandro Lerena'. READ THE PLATE: the transcripts render one clerk's single letterform as Serena, Lorena, Leresa and Lerena on ONE page.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Flores (Uruguay). Civil Death Records 1888-1917
what: Read for its GRANDPARENTS rather than its subject. A Uruguayan civil death act of this period names the deceased's parents and all four grandparents, which makes a death register a pedigree source for people who died long before it. One act placed three families at once. CAUTION RECORDED: no birth years were taken from the stated ages, because the act's own date was not read - only the book's range - and an age without a date is not a birth year.
note: NO WAYPOINT - full-text image ark only, recorded in the url. Found by the exact phrase 'Alejandro Lerena'.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Flores (Uruguay). Civil Birth Records 1887-1902, and San Jose de Mayo Religious Death Records 1839-1851
what: Searched the exact phrase of a GRANDMOTHER's name - 'Casimira Montano' - rather than any of her descendants. ACROSS THE WHOLE CORPUS IT RETURNS 123 HITS AND ONLY TWO ARE URUGUAYAN, which is what a distinctive married-surname pair does: almost no noise, and the two hits are both the right family. One was a birth act naming her as a grandmother with her age, widowhood and STREET ADDRESS; the other, in the San Jose burial register, a daughter of hers dead at seven days in 1850. A HAZARD WORTH CARRYING ACROSS ARCHIVES: the infant buried in 1850 bears her grandmother's forename, and a later woman of that same forename is listed elsewhere as a candidate child of the same couple. Reusing a dead infant's name was ordinary practice and is a standing duplicate hazard in any family that did it.

src: FamilySearch - Santiago Apostol y San Nicolas (Iglesia Matriz de Mendoza), Argentina. Baptism Records 1899-1901
what: THE METHOD IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: to trace a man who is only a name on his son's army card, search the record index for HIS SURNAME plus HIS WIFE'S SURNAME. A distinctive married-in surname (here CARNIGLIA) cuts a whole-corpus crowd to three records in one query, and each is a child. The first act read gave the parents' NATIONALITY - 'orientales' - which is what the whole search was for, and a Lerena godfather standing by proxy besides. NOTE FOR ANYONE FOLLOWING: this image has NO AI transcript, so the full-text route returns nothing for it; it had to be read off the plate.
note: WAYPOINT CHECKED BEFORE BEING RECORDED, as the atlas requires: Q633-3DR resolves in fs-volumes-world.json to 'mendoza, 1899-1903, Bautismos 1899-1903', and the act is 6 January 1900 - inside the range. The waypoint was taken from the film viewer's wc= parameter, which this archive's other work has almost never carried. HOW TO GET FROM AN INDEX HIT TO THE PLATE: the index record's 'Document Information' panel gives Digital Folder, Microfilm and Image numbers; /search/film/<DGS>?i=<N-1> then resolves, and the page TITLE carries both the image ark and the wc= waypoint.

src: FamilySearch - Santiago Apostol y San Nicolas (Iglesia Matriz de Mendoza), Argentina. Baptism Records 1901-1903
what: THE FINDING IS ABOUT THE FORM, NOT THE FAMILY, AND IT TRANSFERS: this parish switched from PROSE to a PRINTED FORM between 1900 and 1902, and the printed form carries a 'natural de' BLANK beside each parent. The prose act of 1900 could only say the parents were 'orientales'; the form of 1902 names the city - MONTEVIDEO - for both. SO WHEN A PARISH ADOPTS A PRINTED REGISTER, GO BACK AND RE-ASK THE QUESTIONS THE PROSE COULD NOT ANSWER. Same couple, same parish, two years apart, and the second act answers what the first could not.
note: NO WAYPOINT RECORDED FOR THIS ONE, DELIBERATELY. The film page offers wc=Q633-3DR, which was verified for item 001 (mendoza, Bautismos 1899-1903) - but this act is in ITEM 003 of the same film, a different volume titled 'Baptism Records 1901-1903', and a film page's wc= describes only its default segment. The year range would fit, and a range that fits is not a confirmed match. Film number recorded instead. ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the index's Digital Folder number carries the item - 004597291_003_M9CV-FLX - and /search/film/<DGS>?i=N resolves against ITEM 001 only, so it silently lands on the wrong volume. Use the index record's own VIEW ORIGINAL DOCUMENT button, which goes to the right image ark.

src: FamilySearch - Valparaiso, Chile. Civil Registration, Death Records September-December 1894
what: REACHED WITHOUT LOOKING FOR IT. A parent-pair query aimed at ARGENTINA - surname LERENA with spouse surname DIAZ - returned Chilean civil registrations, because the family crossed the Andes. CHILE HAD NEVER BEEN A PLACE THIS ARCHIVE READ A RECORD IN; it existed here only as a surname-distribution figure and a DNA probe. THE TRANSFERABLE POINT: a parent-pair query is not constrained by country, and a family that lived at Mendoza is one mountain pass from Valparaiso - so an Argentine search should expect Chilean hits and not discard them. The Chilean death form gives the deceased's nationality, age, address, cause and cemetery, and BOTH PARENTS' NAMES - but never asks where the parents were born.
note: NO WAYPOINT RECORDED. The film page offers wc=MLKY-SPJ with three segment ids; it was not checked against the atlas's volume data and is therefore not written down, on the rule that a film page's wc= describes only its default segment. Film number recorded instead. ALSO: the FamilySearch index estimates this child's birth as 1894 from the death year, where the act says 'diez meses' - about November 1893. An estimated birth year derived from a death year is not a birth year.

src: FamilySearch record index - the two remaining untraced fathers of army drawer Cajon 985, worked to a controlled null
what: ATTEMPTED AND WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY. Searches for LEANDRO LORENA (wife LLANOS) and CONCEPCION LERENA were run on a FamilySearch session that had SILENTLY SIGNED OUT. A signed-out search returns a restricted fuzzy tier - twenty-one rows of United States census for every query, whatever the constraint - and the page says so in one line above the results: 'Create a free account or sign in to see all available results.' NOTHING IS ESTABLISHED ABOUT EITHER MAN.
note: HOW IT WAS CAUGHT, AND IT IS THE ONLY PART WORTH CARRYING: the control was run BEFORE the null and not after. The same spouse-pair query on CARNIGLIA returned three true hits earlier that day - two of whose acts were read off the plate - and returned nothing at all an hour later. ON ANY SIGNED-IN SERVICE A CONTROL MUST BE RE-RUN AFTER THE NULL IT PROTECTS, because the session can change state in between. The cheapest detector is the page header: the account name, or the words 'sign in to see all available results'. This archive already held this trap as false-zero disguise seventeen, 'THE SESSION THAT LOGGED ITSELF OUT AND DID NOT SAY SO', and walked into it anyway. SUPERSEDED: both searches were redone signed in on 10 October and are recorded in the row below.

src: FamilySearch - Libro de matrimonios: Crespo, Entre Rios, Argentina. Marriage Records 1924
what: THE SAME LESSON AS MENDOZA, IN ANOTHER PROVINCE: GO WHERE THE FORM ASKS THE QUESTION. A Chilean death register of 1894 named this man's son and wife but never asks where a PARENT was born; an Entre Rios marriage form of 1924 has a 'de nacionalidad' blank beside each parent, and it answered in one line - ESPANOLA for the father, PERUANA for the mother. When a man cannot be placed from one record class, the question is not whether to search harder but WHICH FORM ASKS WHAT YOU WANT TO KNOW. Argentine civil MARRIAGE acts of this period carry the parents' nationality; BIRTH and DEATH acts of the same provinces often do not.
note: NO WAYPOINT: reached through the index record's VIEW ORIGINAL DOCUMENT button, which returns an image ark without a wc= parameter, and no film number is exposed on that route either - so both fields are left null rather than guessed. A SECOND USE OF THE SAME ACT: the father also signed as a WITNESS, with his own age, marital state and residence, which is how a man who appears only as a name in the parents' line acquired a birth decade. ON ANY MARRIAGE ACT, READ THE WITNESS LIST - the same person can appear twice with different facts attached.

src: FamilySearch - the last two fathers of Cajon 985, re-run signed in; and Fichas dactiloscopicas: Distrito Militar 3, Military Fingerprint Cards 1927-1936
what: ONE TRUE NULL AND ONE RECORD THAT WAS NEVER A NULL. Leandro Lorena with wife LLANOS: the constraint binds signed in and returns eleven rows carrying that surname across five countries, and exactly one is this couple - the army card itself. No baptism, marriage or civil registration anywhere. Concepcion Lerena: her son's MILITARY FINGERPRINT CARD was found in a DIFFERENT DRAWER and a different record class from the enrolment fichas, reached through the person rather than through the drawer. THE PLATE CORRECTED THE INDEX THREE TIMES: surname LERENA not Serena (his own signature); NO FATHER - the field is struck through with a pen, where the index invents 'Spouses Carlos' from the son's own forename; and birthplace CAP. FEDERAL, not Mendoza.
note: THE CONTROL WAS RE-RUN AFTER THE NULL THIS TIME, not only before it - which is the rule the earlier withdrawal bought. FOR ANY ARCHIVE USING ARGENTINE MILITARY RECORDS: there is more than one drawer and more than one record class. Cajon 985 holds enrolment fichas; Distrito Militar 3 holds FINGERPRINT cards with a different form and different fields. A person absent from one may sit in the other, and the way in is a person search, not a drawer walk. AND THE FORM ITSELF IS EVIDENCE: these clerks CANCELLED a parent they did not know rather than leaving the line blank, so a parent's name on one of these cards was positively supplied.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - the compound surname 'Lerena Pelaez', worked to exhaustion across the whole corpus
what: FOUR DOCUMENTS IN THE ENTIRE FULL-TEXT CORPUS, AND EVERY ONE WAS OPENED. The search was aimed at the Montevideo DISPENSATION series and found no dispensation at all; it found four Uruguayan death and confirmation acts that between them name three generations. THE BIGGEST: a Flores death act of 1911 giving a woman of NINETY-TWO as 'hija legitima de Don RAMON LERENA y de Dona MARIA GONZALEZ' - confirming, from the civil register, a parentage a priest had drawn in a kinship diagram fifty-three years earlier. TWO SEPARATE RECORD SYSTEMS, ONE COUPLE. It also named her four surviving children, three of whom this archive held as separate people from separate acts.
note: WALKED: the phrase returns four documents and all four were read, which is why this claims walked for the SEARCH and not for any volume. THE TRANSFERABLE POINT: a COMPOUND surname is a far sharper handle than either half, and it reaches women, who are otherwise invisible to a father-line surname search - three of the four acts here are about women. A WARNING FOR THIS SERIES: the Flores volume titled 'Death Records March 1918-January 1919' contains acts of 1926, so the date range in a volume title is not a bound on its contents. AND A STATED AGE BEAT AN INFERRED ONE BY ELEVEN YEARS: this archive had reasoned the woman's birth to about 1830 from a daughter's age; the act says ninety-two.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - the Montevideo compound surnames: 'Lerena Villademoros', 'Lerena Salvanach'
what: The second half of a work-list row asking for compound surnames to be crossed with the Montevideo dispensation series. NEITHER REACHED A DISPENSATION. 'Lerena Salvanach' returns ZERO in full text - controlled by 'Lerena Villademoros' run minutes earlier in the same session, which returns one. THAT ONE WAS WORTH THE SEARCH: a Buenos Aires baptism of 1918 putting the Villademoros branch in the Argentine capital with a husband, an address and a daughter.
note: A NAME TRAP WORTH RECORDING FOR ANY ARCHIVE WORKING BOTH COUNTRIES: the parish here is SAN JOSE DE FLORES in BUENOS AIRES CITY, which is a different FLORES from the Uruguayan department this archive spends most of its time in, and from the SAN JOSE where the Lerenas married in 1825 and 1837. Three unrelated places sharing two names. AND A CAUTION ON THE IDENTIFICATION: the mother's stated age of thirty-six implies a birth about 1881, where this archive holds her baptism of 19 September 1876. A stated age on a baptism act is the parent's own account and is often short; the identification rests on the rare compound surname and Uruguayan birth, not on the age, and the conflict is recorded rather than smoothed.

src: FamilySearch - Uruguay Civil Registration 1879-2020, Montevideo deaths 1913 (certificate 553), by spouse surname: Lerena x Zalduando
what: Work-list row 186 - who was the 'Zalduando' that a Lerena woman married. NO WAYPOINT ESTABLISHED: reached by index ark, not through a browse path, so no wc=/owc= was ever seen, and DGS 008165206 does not appear in the atlas's volume data. note: THE RESULT WAS NOT A NEW FAMILY BUT A DUPLICATE OF ONE ALREADY HELD. A plate outranks an index, and this index writes Lerena as 'Lerma', so ZALSAMENDI is taken as the better surname reading while the forename is left open. src: FamilySearch - San Juan Bautista, Pocitos, Montevideo: baptism register 1895-1904, folio 344, THE PLATE RE-READ

src: FamilySearch - Uruguay, Civil Registration 1879-2020: Montevideo marriages 1896-1897, act 83, THE PLATE
what: The marriage of Eduardo Zalduondo and Angelica Maria Lerena Villademoros, 20 November 1897 - the act that work-list row 186 had wanted since 27 September and that this archive had recorded as missing the same morning.
note: THE METHOD IS THE POINT AND IT IS EMBARRASSINGLY SIMPLE: SEARCH THE GROOM, NOT THE BRIDE. Every earlier attempt went through the Lerena surname and its manglings - Lerma, Lorena, Zerena - and reached only the death and the children. A single search on the surname ZALDUANDO, with no given name and no date, returned the marriage in the first ten rows, plus a BROTHER (Juan Jose Zalduando Pou, d. 1949, same parents) and a niece. A rare surname searched bare beats a common surname searched cleverly. WHAT THE ACT GAVE: an exact birth date for the groom (15 August 1860); the death of the bride's father AVELINO EDUARDO LERENA TRAIBEL in CANELONES in 1895, which this archive did not have; both Zalduondo parents' nationality from the form's own blank - Juan ORIENTAL, Dolores BRASILENA, against a row that had reasoned 'Catalan or Balearic' from her surname; a witness who is the bride's uncle by marriage; and a BLANK 'Legitiman' line that places all three children after November 1897. NO WAYPOINT ESTABLISHED: reached by index ark, no wc=/owc= seen.

src: FamilySearch - Uruguay, Catholic Church Records 1726-2000 and Civil Registration: VILLADEMOROS searched bare, then Elisa Villademoros

Lerena and Elisa Villademoros is NOT IN THE INDEXED CORPUS from either spouse's side, under Lerena, Serena, Villademoros or Villademeros. Pero' beside Elisa, almost certainly the couple standing godparents - computer-indexed, not opened, recorded as a lead.

src: FamilySearch - Uruguay Catholic Church Records 1726-2000 and Civil Registration 1879-2020: birthplace = Trinidad, Flores, surname Lerena, pages 1-4
what: Work-list row 188 - finishing a sweep begun 27 September 2026 that had taken only the first page of results. Four pages read, about eighty results, all Trinidad-exact rows examined.
note: THE LESSON FOR ANY SWEEP: THE FIRST PAGE IS BAPTISMS AND THE LATER PAGES ARE MARRIAGES. The September pass stopped at page one and came away with children; pages two to four carried the acts that explain them. A DOUBLE WEDDING ON 25 APRIL 1889 - two Lerena sisters marrying two Cardozo brothers at Santisima Trinidad, thirteen months after their brother married those brothers' sister - supplies both blood paths behind the 1911 dispensation of Custodio Lerena and Ema Cardozo, whose own marriage act (18 September 1911) also turned up, converting an inference into a document. Seven people new to the register, including a second Lerena-married-a-Lerena couple and a son of the 1837 Colla couple marrying at Trinidad in 1882. ONE RECORD WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN: a Trinidad birth and death of September 1980 naming a living generation's parents. This archive names living people and gives no dates, places or photographs. ALL INDEX ONLY - not one act was opened. NO WAYPOINT: a search, not a volume.

src: FamilySearch - Uruguay (all collections): the Lerena FORENAME searches - Manuel, Olegaria, Estefania, Felicia
what: Work-list row 187 - four findmypast households this archive could not place, and three Lerena women recorded as MOTHERS at San Jose whom a father-line surname search cannot see.
note: SEARCHING BY FORENAME IS WHAT A FATHER-LINE SURNAME SEARCH CANNOT DO, AND IT ANSWERED MOST OF A ROW THAT HAD STOOD A FORTNIGHT. Four searches - Manuel, Olegaria, Estefania, Felicia - against the Uruguayan corpus. FELICIA LERENA married at San Jose de Mayo on 19 December 1874, daughter of MAURICIO LERENA and CASIMIRA MONTANO: a second child of the 1837 Colla couple, and the explanation for a 'San Jose mother' of 1875. ESTEFANIA LERENA married SERVANDO GONZALEZ and her six children are indexed GONZALEZ LERENA - invisible to a Lerena father-line search, visible the moment the compound is used. OLEGARIA LERENA still has exactly one record and no husband. The MANUEL search separated three men by their mothers' surnames - LERENA MONTANO, LERENA LEONARD, LERENA MARINO - and turned up a civil registration of the 1882 Trinidad marriage filed at SAN JOSE, a departmental conflict recorded and not resolved. A HYPOTHESIS WAS RAISED AND WITHDRAWN WITHIN THE HOUR: that Juana Ferreiroz was a misreading of Juana Galarza. Two independent collections name her Ferreiroz, so it is not a misreading. ALL INDEX ONLY; no act opened.

src: FamilySearch - Uruguay (all collections): forename sweeps for EMILIO and ALEJANDRO Lerena
what: The two men work-list row 137 had listed as unworked since 17 September 2026 - Emilio Lerena and Alejandro F. Lerena, both met as FATHERS in a sweep of the Uruguayan interior.
note: NEITHER NAME WAS ONE MAN, WHICH IS THE RESULT. 'Emilio Lerena' is at least three: a Spanish immigrant from Logrono already held here, a boy born at Trinidad on 2 January 1906 to Florencio P. Lerena Fernandez and Juana Recuero, and an older Emilio married to PAULA CASARES whose son has a marriage registration at Flores in 1931 - the last being the father the sweep had met. The three are separated by arithmetic and by a passenger list, because the Uruguayan civil registration INDEX CARD series 1900-1937 carries no birth dates and no ages at all. 'Alejandro F. Lerena' survives the sweep as a named parent and nothing more: husband of NATALIA LERENA and father of AURORA, with no record of his own among 533 Uruguayan Alejandro hits. A CAUTION FOR THE NEXT SESSION: the index card collection looks like a census of the whole country and is nearly useless for identity, because it gives names and a department and withholds every date that would let two namesakes be told apart. ALL INDEX ONLY.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - the phrase "Elisa Villademoros"; and the act itself, Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon, Religious Marriage Records 1866-1872
what: Work-list row 185 - the marriage of Alejandro M. Lerena and Elisa Villademoros, which this archive had twice concluded was not in the indexed corpus and would have to be walked by image.
note: THE LESSON IS ABOUT INSTRUMENTS, NOT ABOUT THIS COUPLE. The row was right that the act is absent from the RECORD INDEX, and it was searched for there under Lerena, Serena and Villademoros, all controlled. It is present in the FULL-TEXT CORPUS, which is a separate index built by reading page images rather than by transcribing entries, and a single phrase search found it in one attempt. A NULL IN ONE FAMILYSEARCH INDEX IS NOT A NULL IN FAMILYSEARCH. THE ACT, 28 December 1871 at the Cordon: Alejandro MAXIMO Lerena, soltero, natural de Montevideo, son of Avelino and Ambrosia Traibel, married Elisa Villademoros, of the same status and origin, daughter of THE LATE Pedro and Angelica Villademoros; two conciliar banns dispensed by the Obispo Vicario Apostolico; witnesses Dr Joaquin Requena and the groom's own mother. IT PROVES A SISTERHOOD THIS ARCHIVE HAD CALLED 'PROBABLE' FOR A MONTH, and with it that TWO LERENA BROTHERS MARRIED TWO VILLADEMOROS SISTERS - the same double-sibling structure found at Trinidad the same day, a generation earlier and in another department. It does NOT give the groom's age, which is what the row wanted most, and that is said plainly.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - "Sancho Llerena"; and the marriage investigation file of Florentino Gomez, Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Canelones, 1776-1806
what: Re-testing work-list row 26's controlled null on Sancho Llerena's death against the full-text corpus, a different instrument from the record index that produced the null.
note: HIS DEATH IS STILL NOT FOUND. WHAT WAS FOUND IS HIS VOICE. Four pages of full-text hits for the phrase 'Sancho Llerena', one of them the marriage investigation of FLORENTINO GOMEZ before the Juzgado Eclesiastico of Canelones, where SANCHO LLERENA IS A SWORN WITNESS AND DEPOSES IN THE FIRST PERSON - a role no index had ever shown him in, because the record index catalogues principals and parents and this man was neither. HE STATES THAT HE HAD 'ANDADO EN LA LINEA DE VITORIA ALGUNOS ANOS' and knew the groom there. What that line is is NOT established and is deliberately not guessed: a 'linea' in the Rio de la Plata is usually a military frontier, and Vitoria is also a Basque city and a common Brazilian and Spanish place name. The archive's open question on whether this family is Basque or Extremaduran is NOT advanced by it. HIS AGE IS ON THE NEXT FRAME, which is where a deposition states it and which has not been opened - a cheap, named follow-up. THE GENERAL RESULT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE PARTICULAR ONE: the record index and the full-text corpus are two instruments, and three of this archive's standing nulls were only ever tested in one of them.

src: FamilySearch - Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Canelones: Religious Marriage Investigation Files 1776-1806, DGS 008166573 item 8, images 340-341
what: The continuation frame of Sancho Llerena's sworn deposition, opened to look for his age - the named follow-up recorded an hour earlier.
note: HIS AGE IS NOT ON IT, AND THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE DOCUMENT RATHER THAN A FAILED SEARCH. The witness before him closes in the standard form - 'dijo ser mayor de cuarenta y ocho anos' - so this file states ages when it has them and for Sancho it does not. Recorded so nobody opens this frame again hoping. WHAT IT GIVES INSTEAD: SANCHO LLERENA COULD NOT WRITE. His declaration ends 'que dijo NO SABER ESCRIVIR, y la firmo su merced conmigo el presente Notario' - the judge signed in his place. This archive has held him since its first week and had never known anything about the man rather than his relationships. A NAVIGATION TRAP WORTH THE NEXT SESSION'S TIME: an image ark PINS one image and ?i=N is silently IGNORED when an ark is present - three attempts were wasted on it. The route that worked is the viewer's own image-number box. And /search/film/008166573?i=341 would NOT have worked either: this volume is ITEM 8 of that film, and a film query resolves against item 001, which is the trap this archive already recorded in September.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - "Pablo Armando Lerena", "Juan Carlos Lerena", with the control "Rosario de Santa Fe"
what: The question this archive exists to answer, put to the full-text corpus after that instrument had cracked two standing nulls the same day: Pablo Armando Lerena's baptism, and his parents Juan Carlos and Maria Lerena.
note: A NULL THAT THE CONTROL EXPLAINED RATHER THAN MERELY VALIDATED, WHICH IS THE USEFUL KIND. 'Pablo Armando Lerena' returns ZERO. 'Juan Carlos Lerena' returns two, both Uruguayan - the Montevideo dispensation this archive already holds, and a Montevideo death of 2001. THE CONTROL WAS RUN AFTER THE NULL: 'Rosario de Santa Fe' returns 245 pages, so the instrument works and it does reach ARGENTINA. BUT THE ARGENTINE HOLDINGS IT SURFACES ARE BUENOS AIRES PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES, SHIP INSPECTION FILES AND NOTARIAL RECORDS - NOT SANTA FE PARISH REGISTERS. So this is a COVERAGE null, not an absence, and it says nothing about whether the Rosario act exists. Without that control the same zero could have been written up as a third independent confirmation that the baptism is not there. IT ALSO OPENED A RECORD CLASS THIS ARCHIVE HAS NEVER TOUCHED - Buenos Aires probate and ship inspection files, which are indexed by CASE TITLE and so are invisible to the record index and reachable only by full text.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - "Lerena" filtered to ARGENTINA (700 results), first 20 read
what: Opening work-list row 200 - the Buenos Aires probate, notarial and ship-inspection seam, a record class this archive had never touched, found while running a control an hour earlier.
note: THE SHAPE OF THE SEAM: 'Lerena' returns 44,012 full-text results worldwide, 9,516 in South America, 700 in ARGENTINA. The largest Argentine collection by far is BUENOS AIRES CITY LEGAL 1522-2011 with 503 - probate estate case files and notarial records, which are indexed by CASE TITLE and therefore invisible to the record index. Catholic Church Records give 12, Migrations 20, Civil Registration 3. THERE IS NO SANTA FE COLLECTION AT ALL, which is why the Rosario baptism cannot be found here and why that null means nothing. THREE LEADS IN THE FIRST TWENTY: a RAMON LERENA signing as ALCALDE in a Buenos Aires probate file of 1800; a VICENTE LERENA DIAZ keeping the civil register at Pueblo Brugo, Parana, ENTRE RIOS in 1938 - the compound matching Arturo Lerena Garcia x Amalia Diaz; and SPANISH-BORN Eloy, Felisa and Gregorio Lerena in San Jose de Flores baptisms of 1909-1912, where this archive holds a Felisa and a Gregorio from passenger lists and nothing else. ALL ARE OCR SNIPPETS AND NO ACT WAS OPENED; no register rows were created from them. A PRACTICAL NOTE FOR THE NEXT SESSION: the Place filter is behind an 'Expand Place' button and its checkboxes are off-canvas to a click, but once applied the filter is in the URL above and can be reused directly.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - San Jose de Flores, Comuna 7, Buenos Aires City: Baptism Records 1912, act No. 461
what: Turning the first of row 200's three snippet leads into a reading - the Spanish-born Lerenas at a Buenos Aires parish, where this archive holds people who are passenger-list names and nothing else.
note: A SNIPPET BECAME AN ACT, AND THE ACT IS BETTER THAN THE SNIPPET PROMISED. Juana, born 25 June 1912, baptised 10 November 1912, HIJA LEGITIMA of ELOY LERENA, natural de Espana, 26, and FELISA LERENA, natural de Espana, 21; godparents GREGORIO LERENA and ROSA DEFENARI. BOTH PARENTS ARE LERENAS - a fifth Lerena-married-a-Lerena couple for this register, and the first that is Spanish and urban rather than Uruguayan and rural. IT WAS NOT MERGED WITH THE CEMLA ARRIVALS AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING. This archive holds a Felisa and a Gregorio Lerena who landed together at Buenos Aires on 7 December 1911 off the INDIANA from Barcelona, and nothing else about either. A Felisa and a Gregorio appear in this parish eleven months later. But the act makes Felisa 21, so born about 1891, where the 1911 list says 1893 - and the archive's OTHER Felisa, who arrived in 1923, is recorded 1891 exactly. And the roles do not line up: the 1911 pair travelled TOGETHER, while here Gregorio is the GODFATHER and the husband is ELOY, who is on no passenger list held here. THREE NEW PEOPLE - Eloy, Juana and Rosa Defenari. The other two leads of row 200, the 1800 alcalde probate and the 1938 Entre Rios registrar, remain unopened snippets.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City, Probate Estate Case Files 1800 (image group #107093472, item 12)
what: The second of row 200's three leads - a Ramon Lerena signing as alcalde in 1800, opened to find out what jurisdiction he held.
note: HE IS 'ALCALDE DE LA SANTA HERMANDAD DEL PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO', signing on 6 NOVEMBER 1800 in the estate of DON CLEMENTE GARCIA and notifying the widow DONA CELESTINA GONZALEZ about inventories left to a minor. He certifies 'A FALTA DE ESCRIBANO PUBLICO NI REAL, POR NO HABERLO EN ESTA JURISDICCION' - there was no notary in the district, which says something plain about how thinly governed that country was. AND HE SIGNS HIS OWN NAME TWICE, where Sancho Llerena nine years earlier could not. THE PLACE IS INDICATED AND NOT PROVED, which is the whole difficulty. This archive's Ramon Lerena is 'of Rosario-Colla, fl. c.1800-1820' and sits at the apex of the 1858 Trinidad kinship diagram; the date fits exactly. The file mentions a 'vecindad del partido ORIENTAL', pointing at the Banda Oriental and so at Rosario Oriental in Colonia. BUT there is a Partido del Rosario on the Argentine side too, the probate was administered at Buenos Aires which had jurisdiction over both banks, and the OCR around the word ORIENTAL is broken so the sentence cannot be read whole. NOT MERGED. ONE FRAME OF 249 WAS READ. An alcalde's jurisdiction is normally stated in full somewhere in a file like this, so the test is to read on - and a probate file is exactly the record class that names heirs and neighbours.

src: FamilySearch - resuming work-list row 200 (Buenos Aires legal files); the 1800 probate's next frame and the Argentina-filtered full-text search

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City, Probate Estate Case Files 1800, images 28-30 of 249 (item 12)
what: Work-list row 200 - reading on in the probate Ramon Lerena presided over, for the inventory itself and the people in the room.
note: WHAT THE DEAD MAN WAS: A STOREKEEPER WITH A MILL. The first item appraised is a rancho of twenty-two varas by seven, stone walls rendered and whitewashed both sides, FOUR DWELLINGS, one of them a PULPERIA with counter, shelving, back-shop, parlour and bedroom. Then a house of six doors and five windows at 746 pesos; a stone-walled thatched building at 314; and an ATAHONA - a mill - with its wheel, stones, palo-fierro and lantern at 310. THE PEOPLE: the two sworn appraisers are DON BARTHOLO GARCIA and ANDRES BRIVAQUI, who took an oath on a cross before Ramon Lerena. A new witness, LUIS POCHEZ. And CELESTINA GONZALEZ COULD NOT WRITE - 'no firmo porque dijo no saber' - so her husband signed for her. THAT IS THREE PEOPLE IN ONE DAY'S READING WHO COULD NOT SIGN, against Ramon Lerena who signed twice. A CORRECTION TO THIS MORNING: the 'Don Bartolo. Partia' entered from image 26 is almost certainly BARTHOLO GARCIA of image 29 - same forename, same room, same business, five days apart. NOT RENAMED, because this archive does not rename a person on a probable reading of a mangled transcript; the test is to open both frames as images. STILL NOT FOUND: the minor son's name. He is 'su hijo menor' throughout.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Libro de defunciones: Pueblo Brugo, Departamento Parana, Entre Rios, Death Records 1938
what: The last of row 200's three snippet leads, opened - a VICENTE LERENA DIAZ apparently keeping a civil register in Entre Rios.
note: HE IS THE JEFE DEL REGISTRO CIVIL OF PUEBLO BRUGO. The acts open and close in his name: 'ante mi VICENTE LERENA DIAZ, de Registro Civil, comparecio...' and 'Ante mi: Vicente Lerena Diaz'. A LERENA HOLDING PUBLIC OFFICE 138 YEARS AFTER RAMON LERENA WAS ALCALDE AT THE ROSARIO - and both men kept records where the state was thin. A STRONG CANDIDACY, NOT MERGED: Arturo Lerena Garcia and Amalia Diaz had sons surnamed LERENA DIAZ, and this register holds two - Juan Fernando, dead at ten months at Valparaiso in 1894, and ANTONIO, who MARRIED AT CRESPO, DEPARTAMENTO DE PARANA, ENTRE RIOS in 1924. Vicente keeps the register of PUEBLO BRUGO in the SAME DEPARTMENT fourteen years later. A rare compound, a small department, the right generation. The act gives him no parents and no age, so it is not merged. AND A HARDER PAIR CAME WITH IT: this register already held a VICENTE ANTONIO LARENA at GUALEGUAYCHU, also Entre Rios, a father in 1906 and 1913. NOT MERGED AND NOT EXCLUDED - the spelling is no separation here and neither is the department. A BOUNDARY WAS ADDED TO YESTERDAY'S RULE BECAUSE OF THIS RECORD. He signed a volume of 113 images of other people's deaths; read literally, 'everyone named on an act we read' would fill this register with strangers a Lerena merely wrote down. The act must be ABOUT one of our people, or our person a party or witness to it. Where he is only the official of record, the office is recorded and the business of the office is not.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Garcia, Clemente: Buenos Aires City, PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1794 (119 images)
what: Paging past the first 20 Argentina full-text hits for Lerena - looking for anything older than the 1800 court order.
note: THE OLDEST DATED APPEARANCE OF A LERENA IN THIS ARCHIVE, AND THE ONLY ONE THAT SHOWS A MAN'S STANDING RATHER THAN HIS OFFICE. Don GERONIMO ALONSO and Don RAMON LERENA are 'sujetos NOMBRADOS POR LA VIUDA para contar y tasar el ganado y caballos' of the estancia of the late Don Clemente Garcia; they are sworn separately and sign where there is no notary. SO IN 1794 HE IS NOT THE ALCALDE - he is a man a widow chooses to value her stock, and by 1796 he holds the office. A CAREER, not a date. IT ALSO CORRECTS THIS ARCHIVE: Clemente Garcia is 'EL FINADO' here and Celestina Gonzalez 'LA VIUDA', so he died before 1794, not by 1800, and the 1800 case is a second reckoning of an estate already inventoried once. The estate includes an ESTANCIA with cattle and horses as well as the pulperia, the atahona and the house. FOUR PEOPLE ADMITTED: Geronimo Alonso [de Villagomez], Lorenzo Martinez de Olalla (named by the widow to act for her), Guillermo Hurtado de Villagomez and Fulgencio de los Santos, all witnesses or appraisers to an act Ramon Lerena was a PARTY to.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Chabo, Manuel; Agaichu, Maria Marta: Buenos Aires City, PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1796
what: Same result set - any other case closed by the alcalde of the Partido del Rosario, to date the office rather than the man.
note: THE OFFICE IS NOW DATED 1796-1800, NOT ONE YEAR. The auto closes 'lo proveyo, mando y firmo D. RAMON LERENA, ALCALDE DE LA SANTA HERMANDAD DEL PARTIDO DEL ROSARIO... octubre de mil setecientos noventa y seis'. THE PARTIES ARE DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS REGISTER. Ramon Lerena is the official of record here and nothing more, which is exactly the boundary written into tools/check-people-named.py the previous day; admitting Manuel Chabo and Maria Marta Agaichu would make this a register of everyone a Lerena ever wrote down. WHAT THE CASE IS ABOUT IS RECORDED ON HIS OWN ROW, because it is the only business of his office this archive has read apart from the Garcia estate: a power of attorney challenged on the ground that the wife, raised without instruction beside her Guarani parents, did not understand what she had signed and may have been frightened into it.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Registros Consulares: Buenos Aires City, NOTARIAL RECORDS 1900-1901, 395 images
what: Results 41-60 of the 700 Argentina full-text hits for Lerena - still looking for Juan Carlos and Maria.
note: A SOURCE CLASS THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER TOUCHED: the Spanish consulate in Buenos Aires kept its own notarial register, and Spaniards in the city appear in it with their VILLAGE of origin and a consular roll number - detail no Argentine civil act gives. THE FIND IS A HOUSEHOLD WHO CARRY THE NAME TWICE. Prudencio Benito and Juan Jose LERENA Y LERENA, bachelors and shop-assistants of Navarrete, Logrono, consular numbers 950 and 951, give power over the family property in Spain to their widowed mother ISABELA LERENA Y BASARAN and their married brother JOSE DOLORES LERENA Y LERENA. AND THE FIRST NOTE WRITTEN HERE OVERCLAIMED IT, CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR. It said the repeated surname on Pablo Armando's 1908 card had always been the easiest thing to dismiss as a clerical duplication and that this household answered it. THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY HERE FIVE TIMES OVER - two Trinidad couples, the 1911 dispensation, Alejandro, and Eloy x Felisa Lerena at San Jose de Flores in 1912, that last found the same morning. This is the SIXTH, and what it alone adds is a household outside South America, children carrying the name doubled as a surname of record, and a village whose registers can be opened. NO LINK CLAIMED - they are Spanish subjects and every line here is Banda Oriental from the 1790s; recorded on /name/ as a namesake household. IT ALSO PROBABLY IDENTIFIES AN EXISTING ROW: 'Juan Jose LERENA, b.1876, Logrono, soltero, comercio' from CEMLA, landed 1920/1928/1929 - same forenames, province, civil state, trade and city, and 24 years old that November. NOT MERGED: CEMLA records the province, the act records the village. NEXT: the parish registers of Navarrete.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Escalada, Carlos M.; Lerena, Carlos A.: Buenos Aires City, PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1891, 91 images
what: Results 61-80 of the Argentina full-text set - a probate case TITLED with a Lerena, so he is a party and not a mention.
note: CARLOS A. LERENA SUED THE ESTATE OF DON CARLOS MARIA ESCALADA FOR A COMMISSION, February 1890 - 'la demanda entablada por D. Carlos A. Lerena, sobre cobro de pesos', the claim being 'la comision por la compraventa a que se refiere'. The estate's lawyer A. Ferreyra answered that it rests on his bare assertion, that he 'no acompana documento alguno en que conste lo que asevera. NI TAMPOCO PUEDE ACOMPANARLO', and that the succession had concluded no contract. A LERENA WORKING AS A BROKER IN BUENOS AIRES IN 1890 - the right city and the right decade, with nothing tying him to Rosario or to Pablo Armando. Outcome unknown: 91 images, one read. Kept apart from Carlos Lerena of Mendoza in _person-pairs.txt.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Convento de San Francisco; Segura, Placido; Gallegos, Maria Antonia: Buenos Aires City, PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1795
what: Opened because it is from Ramon Lerena's decade - looking for him in a third 1790s Buenos Aires probate.
note: NOT A LERENA AT ALL, AND THE MOST USEFUL NULL OF THE DAY. The transcript reads 'admitio absolutamente LA LERENA' and 'verificarse LA LERENCIA'. The word is HERENCIA - to accept an inheritance, here without benefit of inventory. IN A CORPUS MADE ENTIRELY OF PROBATE FILES, THE COMMONEST WORD IN THE CORPUS IMPERSONATES THIS SURNAME. So the '700 Argentine full-text hits for Lerena' this archive has been paging through is not 700 appearances of a rare name; the real number is unknown and much smaller. Recorded in data/false-zeros.tsv as the first FALSE POSITIVE in a file that until now held only false zeros. GENERAL RULE: before trusting a full-text count, find out what your surname is a misreading of in that language and that document type.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - phrase search "Juan Carlos Lerena", whole corpus, no place filter
what: Re-running the central question as an exact phrase, after learning that single-word Lerena hits in probate files are mostly the word HERENCIA.
note: A CONTROL, NOT A FIND, AND IT PASSED. Two results in the entire corpus, exactly the two this archive found on 15 September: Juan Carlos GONZALEZ LERENA, dispensed the three banns at Montevideo on 8 November 1922 to marry Concepcion Petrona Urbano of the Cordon - already read off the plate on 21 September (film 007713367 image 02860, folio 391, entry 14610) and already excluded, because LERENA is his maternal surname and he is marrying forty years too late; and a 2001 Montevideo death record for Juan Carlos ATAY LERENA. SO THE PHRASE SEARCH REPRODUCES A KNOWN RESULT EXACTLY, which is what a control is for - and a month on, the growing corpus still holds no other Juan Carlos Lerena anywhere in the world.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Expediente: Huergo Aragon, Clemente: Madrid, GOVERNMENT PENSIONS 1896
what: Phrase search "Lerena y Lerena" (27 results) - testing whether the doubled surname found that morning at Navarrete appears anywhere else.
note: IT CONFIRMED AND PROMOTED A MAN ENTERED TWENTY MINUTES EARLIER. The 1900 consular act at Buenos Aires called JOSE DOLORES LERENA Y LERENA merely 'casado y propietario' of Navarrete. This 1896 certificate is signed by him as 'JUEZ MUNICIPAL SUPLENTE DE ESTA VILLA, encargado de la Jurisdiccion por ausencia del propietario, Y TAMBIEN DEL REGISTRO CIVIL DE LA MISMA', certifying from his own book the death at Navarrete on 11 November 1895 of Juan Manuel Chavarri Oteyza of Fuenmayor, aged seventy, at folio 191 of tomo 11 of the Defunciones. NOBODY FROM THAT DEATH ACT IS ADMITTED TO THE REGISTER - he is the official and they are the business of his office, the same boundary applied to Vicente Lerena Diaz's Pueblo Brugo register the day before. NOTE ON THE PHRASE ITSELF: most of the 27 hits are NOT the compound surname but two Lerenas joined by 'and' - 'padrinos Miguel Lerena y Rebeca Lerena' - which is a different and also useful thing, and several of those are at Trinidad, Flores and at the Cordon, Montevideo, this archive's own parishes. Not yet read.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion y San Felipe y Santiago, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo: Baptism Records 13 Feb 1879 - 24 Jul 1880
what: The Uruguayan half of the "Lerena y Lerena" phrase search - 15 results, this one snippeted 'padrinos Avelino Lerena y Adelina Lerena'.
note: THE PHRASE MOSTLY FINDS TWO LERENAS JOINED BY 'AND', NOT THE COMPOUND SURNAME - 'padrinos Avelino Lerena y Adelina Lerena' - AND THAT TURNS OUT TO BE WORTH MORE HERE, because two Lerenas standing together at a font is a relationship. This act is the christening of MARIA ADELINA LERENA LARRIERA, whose row this archive had carried as index-level since 21 September with the ark and nothing read. The names panel gives all four grandparents: AVELINO LERENA and AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, already known as the head of the Lerena Traibel branch, and MIGUEL LARRIERA and CAROLINA CHAVARRIA, WHO WERE NOT KNOWN AT ALL - the parents of Maria Ines Larriera, a woman whose row said 'nothing else in this archive names her' and has now been corrected twice. IT ALSO CORRECTED A GENERATION: her brother ANGEL MIGUEL AVELINO was said to carry his GREAT-grandfather's name, and Avelino is his grandfather - the child is named for BOTH grandfathers, Miguel Larriera and Avelino Lerena. AND THE SURNAME IS SPELLED FOUR WAYS ON ONE PAGE: Lerena, Lerena with a tilde, Serena, Levena. The christening is at the MONTEVIDEO CATHEDRAL although she was born in the Departamento de San Jose.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon, Montevideo: Baptism Records January 1891 - July 1892
what: The Cordon volumes out of the Uruguayan "Lerena y Lerena" results - this family's own parish, unread.
pages: the christening of Balvina Maria Cabrera
note: ONE LERENA ENTRY IN THE VOLUME AND IT IS TWO PEOPLE: 'ADOLFO LERENA' and 'MARIA MERCEDES LERENA' stood godparents together to Balvina Maria, daughter of Manuel Cabrera and Balvina Valdivia. THIS MOVES ADOLFO BACK TWELVE YEARS - this archive had him only as the godfather at Pocitos in August 1903, where it reasoned he was likely a brother of the Lerena woman whose child he stood for. He was an adult at the Cordon by 1891. THE WOMAN IS NEW AND IS NOT MERGED WITH ANY OF THE FOUR MERCEDES ALREADY HERE - Mercedes Micaela Lerena Traibel b.1863, the Catedral godmother of 1880, the Mercedes who married Luis P. Marquez in 1883, and Mercedes Lerena de Martinez of Mendoza 1902. The forename runs through this family too hard to separate anyone, and the names panel gives her no age, no parents and no second surname. THE DATE WITHIN THE VOLUME IS NOT ESTABLISHED: January 1891 to July 1892, read from the names panel rather than the page, so the act itself is still worth opening.

src: FamilySearch - Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion y San Felipe y Santiago, Montevideo: Baptism Records 16 Mar 1840 - 18 Dec 1842, film 007713376 image 01689 (deepzoom apid TH-909-52377-68331-65)
what: Re-reading a plate this archive had already read, because its own page quoted the act with a forename in SQUARE BRACKETS and a second row contradicted it.
note: IT DELETED A PERSON. The act was quoted here as 'Nieto pat[erno de D. DOMINGO] RODRIG.z', and a man - DON DOMINGO RODRIGUEZ (the elder, of la Colonia) - had been built from the words inside those brackets, published, charted and given a wife. Read at 4000px off the deepzoom tile the plate says: 'Nieto Pat.o de D. JOAQUIN RODRIG.z y D.a Juana del Espiritu S.to: ambos nat.s de la Colonia del Sacram.to; y por parte Mat.a de D. SANCHO LERENA y D.a Ma FERNANDEZ'. The act's own names panel independently gives 'Pats. Joaquin Rodriguez'. SO THE GRANDFATHER IS MAYOR DON JOAQUIN RUIZ DE CARVALLO, already in this register under its known second spelling of the surname, and the phantom is withdrawn. THE SAME BRACKET HAD SPLIT ONE WOMAN IN TWO: Juana del Espiritu Santo was entered as the phantom's wife while Juana Suarez sat here as Joaquin's; both are the mother of Capitan Antonio, and they are merged. Two further readings: the godfather is 'D. JOAQUIN SOSA DE CRUZ SECO' and the godmother BALVINA SUAREZ.

src: FamilySearch - Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion y San Felipe y Santiago, Montevideo: Baptism Records 4 May 1825 - 21 Aug 1828, film 007713376 image 00601
what: The control for the read above: the other grandchild's act, to see whether the two acts name the same paternal grandparents.
pages: image 00601, folio 150, the act of 12 May 1827
note: THE CONTROL AGREED, WHICH IS WHAT SETTLED THE MERGE. The names panel of Lucinda Gregoria's baptism gives father Antonio Ruiz de Carvallo, mother Dominga 'Llarena', and the grandparents JOAQUIN RUIZ DE CARVALLO and JUANA SUAREZ beside Sancho Llerena and Maria Fernandez. So BOTH of Antonio's children's baptisms name the same paternal grandfather - Joaquin - and his wife under two names, SUAREZ in 1827 and DEL ESPIRITU SANTO in 1840. One woman, two renderings, one slot. Without this act the merge would have rested on a single reading.

src: FamilySearch - Nuestra Senora de los Desamparados, partido de Adolfo Alsina, Buenos Aires: Baptism Records 12 Apr 1917 - 19 Feb 1923
what: Testing whether the Eduardo Lerena of a Buenos Aires baptism is the Eduardo Lerena dispensed at Montevideo in December 1919 - by reading the daughter's act off the plate instead of the index.
note: THE INDEX WAS WRONG TWICE AND THE PLATE SETTLED BOTH. The surname is RAZZETTI, not Rozzetti - written twice on one line, once for the mother and once for the godfather DOMINGO RAZZETTI - and the event is in the PARTIDO DE ADOLFO ALSINA in Buenos Aires province, not 'Buenos Aires City' as the index normalises it; the act says 'domiciliados en ESTE PARTIDO'. ANA MARIA now has a birth date, 12 January 1921, a baptism a week later, a parish, a priest (JOSE SERRANO LOPEZ) and two godparents. 'HIJA LEGITIMA' means the parents were married before January 1921. AND THE PAIR IT WAS OPENED FOR GOT STRONGER WITHOUT BEING PROVED: the 1919 Montevideo dispensation names a MARIA MERCEDES 'RAZZELLO' of Las Piedras, and RAZZELLO against RAZZETTI is one hand read twice, while the index's ROZZETTI was never on the page. Thirteen months from dispensation to first child. NOT MERGED - no act yet read calls the Buenos Aires man oriental. NEXT: the Montevideo marriage act behind the 1919 dispensation.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon, Montevideo: Baptism Records August 1900 - October 1902
what: The second Cordon volume from the Uruguayan "Lerena y Lerena" results - this family's own parish.
pages: the christening of Juan Eduardo Silva
note: ONE LERENA ENTRY AND IT IS TWO PEOPLE AGAIN: EDUARDO LERENA and 'Ema. Lerena' stood godparents together to Juan Eduardo, son of Juan Silva and Toribia Martinez. The fourth pair of Lerenas at one font found today, after the Montevideo cathedral in 1879, the Cordon in 1891-92 and the Trinidad volumes. NEITHER IS IDENTIFIED. This register now holds four men called Eduardo Lerena and none is merged with another; the Cordon is the parish of the Lerena Traibel, which makes AVELINO EDUARDO LERENA TRAIBEL the nearest candidate and is not an argument, since he is 'Avelino Eduardo' on every act read of him. The godmother could be EMA SIXTA LERENA JUANICO (b.1876) or MARIA EMA LERENA LENGUAS (b.1857) and a third cannot be excluded. AND A BOUNDARY IS RECORDED RATHER THAN SETTLED QUIETLY: the Silva household is NOT admitted to the register. The rule admits everyone named on an act our person is a party to, and a godparent is a party - but a baptism is ABOUT the child's household and a Lerena at the font is a guest at it. The household is named in full on both rows so nothing is lost if the rule is later drawn the other way. The date within the volume is not established: read from the names panel, not the page.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Canelones: MARRIAGE RECORDS 1917-1924, acta No. 4, Santa Lucia, Segunda Seccion
what: Following a NOT MERGED note's own 'what would settle it': the marriage behind the December 1919 dispensation, which would name Eduardo Lerena's parents.
note: IT SETTLED THE PAIR AND NAMED A NEW HOUSEHOLD, FOUR HOURS AFTER THE PAIR WAS WRITTEN. 'En Santa Lucia y el dia ONCE DE ENERO DE MIL NOVECIENTOS VEINTE... comparecen: don EDUARDO LERENA, de nacionalidad ORIENTAL, NACIDO EL DIA VEINTIDOS DE ABRIL DE MIL OCHOCIENTOS OCHENTA Y SEIS EN MONTEVIDEO, de profesion EMPLEADO... hijo de ARTURO LERENA, de nacionalidad oriental, de estado casado, de SESENTA Y DOS anos, domiciliado en MONTEVIDEO, y de EMA REGULES, de nacionalidad oriental... de CINCUENTA Y CINCO anos; y dona MARIA MERCEDES RAZZETTI, de nacionalidad ORIENTAL, NACIDA EL DIA VEINTICINCO DE JULIO DE MIL OCHOCIENTOS NOVENTA Y NUEVE EN COLON... hija de DOMINGO RAZZETTI, de nacionalidad italiano, de CINCUENTA Y NUEVE anos, domiciliado en la CUARTA SECCION de este departamento, y de JOSEFINA BERTOGLIO, de nacionalidad italiana, de CINCUENTA anos'. WHAT PROVES THE MERGE IS NOT THE NAMES BUT HER PARENTS: Domingo Razzetti and Josefina Bertoglio stood godparents to the couple's daughter at Adolfo Alsina, Buenos Aires, on 19 January 1921 - the same four people in two countries thirteen months apart. NEW: ARTURO LERENA, ORIENTAL, born about 1857 and living in Montevideo in 1920, with his wife EMA REGULES - NOT the Spanish Arturo Lerena Garcia this register already holds, and kept apart on nationality. Eduardo gains an exact birth date, which this archive has for very few of its people. Witnesses Alberto Laneri and Francisco Percar, whose surnames the transcript contradicts in the signature line and which are NOT established.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Montevideo: Religious Marriage Records (volume catalogued 1887), the act of 23 June 1880, Basilica Menor y Catedral de Montevideo
what: Searching the two surnames together - Lerena and Regules - to find the marriage that would give Arturo Lerena's own parents.
note: IT REACHED THE TRUNK. 'el DOCTOR DON ARTURO LERENA, natural de esta Republica, soltero, de VEINTE Y DOS ANOS de edad, HIJO LEGITIMO DE DON AVELINO LERENA Y DONA AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, con DONA EMMA REGULES... de DIEZ Y SEIS ANOS, hija legitima de DON WENCESLAO REGULES y DONA JUSTINIANA MELILLA: fueron testigos el DOCTOR DON AMBROSIO LERENA y Dona Justiniana Melilla de Regules', the banns dispensed by Bishop JACINTO VERA himself and the act authorised by the Presbitero JUAN JOSE BRID. SO THE ARGENTINE HOUSEHOLD AT ADOLFO ALSINA IS NOT A NAMESAKE: Eduardo Lerena, who married Maria Mercedes Razzetti at Santa Lucia in 1920 and baptised a daughter in Buenos Aires province in 1921, is a grandson of Avelino Lerena Fernandez and Ambrosia Traibel and a great-grandson of Sancho. ARTURO IS A DOCTOR, and the witness AMBROSIO LERENA is a second doctor of the name and new to this archive - two professional men in one generation, two after Sancho. NOT MERGED WITH JUAN ARTURO LERENA TRAIBEL, born 16 February 1861, whose age does not fit: nineteen against the twenty-two on the act, with the 1920 act agreeing on 1857-58. NEXT: the Montevideo civil marriages of 1907-08 hold a 'Dona EMMA LERENA REGULES' with these same parents - a daughter, marrying - and the Las Piedras religious marriage register 1915-1937 should hold the church half of Eduardo's own wedding.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Montevideo: MARRIAGE RECORDS (volume catalogued 1907-1908), acta No. 16 of 9 August 1909, Sexta Seccion
what: The lead left open last night: a 'Dona Emma Lerena Regules' marrying with Arturo Lerena and Emma Regules as her parents.
note: A SISTER FOR EDUARDO, AND A CORRECTION TO HIS FATHER'S TRADE. EMMA LERENA REGULES, born 18 May 1885 at SAN JOSE, married FERMIN CARLOS DE YEREGUI (born Montevideo 4 November 1879, son of the late Fermin de Yeregui and Mercedes de Melis) on 9 August 1909 before the Juez de Paz Cesar Schiaffino. HER FATHER IS GIVEN AS 'DE PROFESION ABOGADO' - so the 'Doctor Don Arturo Lerena' of the 1880 act is a LAWYER, and this archive's note that he was a doctor is corrected. SO THE HOUSEHOLD WAS AT SAN JOSE IN MAY 1885 AND AT MONTEVIDEO IN APRIL 1886, eleven months apart - tight, and recorded as a tension rather than resolved. IN 1909 THE PARENTS ARE GIVEN AT DIFFERENT ADDRESSES, Colonia 2200 and Colonia 228, both 'de estado casado'; the numbers differ by a factor of ten and a transcriber's slip is likelier than a separation. NOT RESOLVED. AND THE WITNESSES WERE TWO LAWYERS, ONE OF THEM JUAN ZORRILLA DE SAN MARTIN - fifty-three, widower, abogado, of calle Rincon, which is the national poet of Uruguay on every count except a document that says so. Recorded with no inference drawn, as this archive records its president and its bishop.

src: FamilySearch RECORD INDEX - parent-pair query: father ARTURO LERENA, mother EMMA REGULES (Uruguay, Civil Registration 1879-2020; Uruguay, Catholic Church Records 1726-2000)
what: Asking the index for the whole sibship at once, now that a marriage act had named the parents exactly.
note: EIGHT RECORDS, SIX CHILDREN, AND TWO NAMES THAT CORROBORATE THE PARENTAGE. Ema Justina Felicia (b. 18 May 1881, San Jose), Arturo Mario (b. 9 April 1884, San Jose; d. 6 May 1949, Montevideo, wife Maria Juana), Emma (b. 18 May 1885, San Jose - already held from her 1909 marriage act), Eduardo (b. 22 April 1886, Montevideo), CORA MARIA AVELINA (b. 8 June 1887, christened at the Union 23 October 1887) and ROBERTO AMBROSIO (b. 1 November 1896, Montevideo). AVELINA AND AMBROSIO ARE HIS OWN PARENTS' NAMES - Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel - so the 1880 marriage act's parentage is corroborated by the next generation's forenames without opening a second act. THE HOUSEHOLD MOVED: San Jose 1881-1885, Montevideo from 1886. A NINE-YEAR GAP, 1887 to 1896, is not explained. TWO THINGS LEFT UNRESOLVED RATHER THAN TIDIED: Ema Justina Felicia (1881) and Emma (1885) share a birthday, 18 May, in the same department to the same parents - two daughters, a mis-indexed year, or a dead child's name and date reused - and the index gives EDUARDO a birth of 1868 where his own marriage act says 1886, a digit transposition that would have cost a day if it had been believed. ALL INDEX-LEVEL: no act opened.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - Montevideo: DEATH RECORDS 1931-1938, acta No. 8 of 2 March 1936, Tercera Seccion
what: Testing whether Arturo Lerena the abogado is the Juan Arturo Lerena Traibel baptised in 1861 - by finding the one act that would state his age at death.
note: THE BEST DOCUMENT THIS HOUSEHOLD HAS. Arturo Lerena died at TWO IN THE MORNING on 2 MARCH 1936 at TREINTA Y TRES 269, Montevideo, 'de SETENTA Y OCHO ANOS DE EDAD... DE PROFESION ABOGADO... hijo de A[V]ELINO [L]ERENA y de AMBROSIA TR[A]IBEL, AMBOS FALLECIDOS... casado con [E]MA REGULES, de cuyo consorcio quedaron CINCO HIJOS llamados EMA, MARIO, EDUARDO, CORA y ROBERTO'. It confirms his parents a second time and the ABOGADO correction a second time. IT DOES NOT SETTLE THE PAIR, AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING: seventy-eight in March 1936 is a birth of 1857-58, which agrees with twenty-two in June 1880 and sixty-two in January 1920 - three independent statements - against one baptism of a 'JUAN ARTURO' on 16 February 1861. BUT THE DECLARANTS WERE NOT FAMILY, an Italian employee of forty and an oriental of twenty-three, so the age is secondhand like the other two. FAMILYSEARCH'S OWN TREE HAS MERGED THEM ALREADY, attaching this record to 'Juan Arturo Lerena Traibel, 1861-1936'. That is a tree, not a document. THE FIVE SURVIVING CHILDREN NAME ONLY ONE EMA where this register holds two born on 18 May, 1881 and 1885 - which tilts that question without closing it, since five surviving of six is also what the act would say if a sister had died.

src: FamilySearch RECORD INDEX - exact-surname parent-pair query: FATHER surname LERENA with MOTHER surname LERENA, worldwide
what: Asking the record index the one question Pablo Armando's enrolment card asks: which couples were a Lerena father and a Lerena mother?
note: THE MOST USEFUL NULL THIS ARCHIVE HAS RUN ON ITS OWN QUESTION, AND IT CARRIES ITS OWN CONTROL. Pablo Armando's 1908 enrolment card names JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA LERENA - a Lerena father and a Lerena mother. Asked of the record index with both surnames EXACT, that configuration returns THIRTY-EIGHT couples in the whole world, and NOT ONE OF THEM IS A JUAN CARLOS. THE CONTROL IS BUILT IN: the same query returns couples this archive already holds - Eloy Lerena and Felisa Lerena at San Jose de Flores in 1912, Alejandro F. Lerena and Natalia Lerena at Trinidad - so the query finds what it should. NOTE WHICH INDEX THIS IS: the earlier nulls on 'Juan Carlos Lerena' were FULL-TEXT phrase searches, which read words on page images; this is the NAME INDEX, which catalogues parents as fields. Two different indexes, now both empty on the same man. AND IT PRODUCED FOUR URUGUAYAN 'COUPLES' THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER MET - AND THE FIRST ONE OPENED WAS NOT A COUPLE AT ALL. The San Jose de Mayo pair, read off the plate the same day, is 'hijo natural de BARBARA, ESCLAVA DE D.N ALEJANDRO LERENA' - an enslaved woman given her holder's surname by the indexer. SO THE COUNT OF THIRTY-EIGHT IS A COUNT OF INDEX ENTRIES, NOT OF MARRIAGES, and a parent-pair query cannot tell a marriage from a slave-holding. THE SECOND ONE OPENED COLLAPSED THE SAME WAY: the Trinidad pair's mother is 'Dona ANDREA ETCHEBERSE' on the 1906 marriage act, with the surname broken across the page opening, and the index gave her the father's. TWO OF FOUR, ONE MECHANISM - see data/false-zeros.tsv. The remaining two: Antonio Lerena and Sabina Lerena, whose daughter married at San Francisco de Asis in 1865; VITALIANO LERENA and ANDREA LERENA at TRINIDAD, the town this archive has worked hardest; Alejandro Lerena and BARBARA Lerena at San Jose de Mayo in 1846, where the elder Alejandro was living; and Florencio Lerena with a Teresa Lerena, which collides with a Florencio already held here. Seventeen people entered, all index-level. FINAL, 12 OCTOBER 2026: ALL FOUR WERE OPENED AND NOT ONE IS A DEMONSTRATED COUPLE OF TWO LERENAS. Two disproved outright - an enslaved woman given her holder's surname at San Jose de Mayo in 1846, and a mother named ETCHEBERSE whose surname broke across a page opening at Trinidad in 1906. Two unproved - 'Antonio y Sabina SERENA', one surname between two parents, in 1865; and 'Florencio SERENA fallecido... Teresa SERENA, de estado VIUDA' in 1938, where a widow carries her husband's name as a matter of course. THE QUERY IS A GOOD WAY TO FIND LERENA HOUSEHOLDS AND A BAD WAY TO COUNT MARRIAGES. The six couples this archive held before it are untouched, because every one of them rests on an act.

src: FamilySearch - San Jose de Mayo: RELIGIOUS DEATH RECORDS July 1839 - December 1851, the burial of 28 April 1846
what: Opening the first of the four new Lerena-married-a-Lerena couples - the San Jose de Mayo pair of 1846, because an index entry contradicted a man this archive thinks it knows.
note: THE COUPLE DOES NOT EXIST AND THE TRUTH IS WORSE. 'En esta Parroquia de S.n Jose a VEINTE Y OCHO DE ABRIL de mil ochocientos CUARENTA Y SEIS, yo D.n FRAN.CO CASTELLO cura vic.o int.o di sepultura en el ANGELORIO al cadaver de CARMELO ANSELMO, HIJO NATURAL DE BARBARA, ESCLAVA DE D.N ALEJANDRO LERENA, murio ayer de enfermedad, de edad de SIETE DIAS, y se le hizo oficio rezado, de que certifico.' THE INDEXER READ 'esclava de D.n Alejandro Lerena' AS A PARENT PAIR, made Alejandro the father and GAVE BARBARA THE SURNAME OF THE MAN WHO HELD HER. All three rows renamed to what the act says; three addresses retired to redirects the day they were minted. SHE IS THE FIFTH PERSON THIS FAMILY IS KNOWN TO HAVE HELD IN SLAVERY, after JUANA, ANTONIO, JOSE and TERESA in Sancho Llerena's household at Canelones in 1812, and the first outside it - thirty-four years later, a different household, a different department. ON THE DATE THIS ARCHIVE STATES ONLY WHAT IT KNOWS: the act says 'esclava' in April 1846, and which stage of Uruguay's abolition applied at San Jose then is NOT ESTABLISHED HERE. The man is now 'Don Alejandro LERENA (of San Jose de Mayo, 1846)' and is NOT merged with the elder Alejandro who married there in 1825, though the town, the decade and the style of address all fit.

src: FamilySearch - Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores: RELIGIOUS MARRIAGE RECORDS July 1898 - December 1912, the act of 26 March 1906
what: The second of the four new Lerena-married-a-Lerena couples, opened straight after the first one turned out to be an enslaved woman.
note: THE SECOND COUPLE COLLAPSED THE SAME WAY AS THE FIRST. 'el VEINTE Y SEIS DE MARZO [de mil no]vecientos SEIS... contrajo DON ANTONIO ETCHEBERSE, oriental, soltero, de TREINTA Y TRES anos, HIJO [legitimo struck out] NATURAL de Don ANTONIO ETCHEBERSE y de Dona FRAILANA VALIENTE, con Dona ANDREA ALBINA LERENA, oriental, soltera, de TREINTA Y DOS anos, HIJA LEGITIMA DE DON VITALIANO LERENA Y DE DONA ANDREA ETCHEBERSE. Los testigos fueron JOSE MARTINEZ y BERNARDO YRIZA[BAL].' THE MOTHER IS AN ETCHEBERSE, AND HER SURNAME IS BROKEN ACROSS THE PAGE OPENING - 'ANDREA' at the foot of the left page, 'ETCHEBERSE.' at the head of the right. The index gave her the FATHER'S surname, exactly as it gave Barbara her holder's at San Jose de Mayo that morning. FOUR FURTHER CORRECTIONS OFF ONE PLATE: the groom is ETCHEBERSE not Echeberse; he was THIRTY-THREE, not the index's 'tres anos'; the priest STRUCK OUT 'legitimo' AND WROTE 'natural' over his parentage; and the index's marriage date of '26 March 1000' is 1906. WHAT SURVIVES AND IS WORTH HAVING: a VITALIANO LERENA at Santisima Trinidad with a daughter born about 1874 and married there in 1906 - in the town this archive has swept, and in none of the sweeps. The bride's mother shares the groom's surname and the act records no impediment, which is an observation and not a conclusion.

src: FamilySearch - Montevideo: MARRIAGE RECORDS 1938, acta No. 2 of 4 January 1938, 11a seccion
what: The last of the four new Lerena-married-a-Lerena couples, after two had collapsed and one had gone doubtful.
note: NOT DISPROVED AND NOT PROVED, AND IT CLOSED A DIFFERENT QUESTION INSTEAD. The act names VICTORINA SERENA, born 6 March 1908 in the Departamento de CERRO LARGO, 'hija de FLORENCIO SERENA, DE ESTADO FALLECIDO... y de TERESA SERENA, DE ESTADO VIUDA, domiciliada en el Dpto. de CERRO LARGO', marrying JUAN RIBERO, jornalero, born 15 May 1912, both at Esperanza 787. BOTH PARENTS CARRY ONE SURNAME - BUT SHE IS A WIDOW, and a widow is routinely written under her late husband's name, so a couple of two Lerenas is not demonstrated. WHAT IT DID SETTLE: this family is of CERRO LARGO, four departments from Trinidad, so the FLORENCIO LERENA of Trinidad - husband of Juana Recuero - is a different man, and that pair entry is closed by a place rather than left open. TWO CONFLICTS RECORDED AND NOT SMOOTHED: her birth registration at Melo gives 18 MAY 1908 where this act gives 6 MARCH 1908, and that registration names TERESA LLERENA ALONE, with no father - he appears thirty years later, already dead. AND SHE COULD NOT SIGN: 'la contrayente manifiesta NO SABER FIRMAR, verificandolo a su ruego dona CATALINA G. DE GARCIA'.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - phrase search "Doctor Lerena", whole corpus; and Aguirre, Feliciano: Buenos Aires City, PROBATE ESTATE CASE FILES 1889
what: Worklist row 205: the one-line snippet 'lo hace el Doctor Lerena si la', carried with a warning that in this corpus 'lerena' is usually the word HERENCIA.
note: HE IS REAL, AND THE WARNING WAS RIGHT TO BE THERE. The passage: 'no lo hace el DOCTOR LERENA si la intervencion del CONSUL ESPANOL... es o no oportuna. Lo que debe resolverse es si el nombramiento del CURADOR DON LLERENA es o no arreglado a derecho. Al simple pedido de f.46, el Juzgado nombra CURADOR AL DOCTOR LLERENA, sin oir a este Ministerio...' A LAWYER APPOINTED CURADOR OF AN ESTATE, with the Fiscal objecting that the court appointed him without consulting the Ministry or inviting the Spanish consul. THE SAME PASSAGE SPELLS HIM LERENA AND LLERENA, TWICE EACH, IN ONE HAND - the clearest demonstration this register has that the two spellings are one name. AND 'DOCTOR' IS AGAIN THE STYLE OF AN ABOGADO, not a physician, which is the second time in one day. THE PHRASE SEARCH RETURNS 64 HITS AND OPENS THREE SEAMS NOT YET WORKED: the same Doctor Lerena recurs in the Buenos Aires probates of 1890, 1894 and 1897; a DOCTOR LERENA signs medical certificates on Montevideo death records of 1949 and 1967, who IS a physician and is a different man; and the student files of the Universidad de Toledo carry 'Senores Doctor Lerena' in the 1790s-1830s, which is Spain and probably nothing to do with this family.

src: FamilySearch FULL TEXT - the phrase "Lerena y Lerena" filtered to Uruguay: ALL 15 VOLUMES, worklist row 203
what: Worklist row 203: twelve volumes left unread after three were worked on 11 October.
note: ALL FIFTEEN NOW READ, AND THE SEAM'S REAL SHAPE IS CLEAR. The phrase finds TWO LERENAS STANDING TOGETHER, almost always as GODPARENTS, and the pairs are mostly people this register already holds: Bernabe with Alejandrina (Montevideo 1890-91), Bernabe with Natalia (Montevideo 1901-02), Juan with Margarita (Trinidad 1889-94), Vitaliano with Andrea (Trinidad 1886-88, twice), Alejandro with Clorinda (Uruguay 1917-18). THREE THINGS WORTH MORE THAN THE PAIRS. (1) A 'MONTEVIDEO' VOLUME IS NOT A MONTEVIDEO ACT: the 1890-91 page is the capital's CIVIL register transcribing a parish certificate signed by the Cura Vicario Brana 'en TRINIDAD a catorce de [noviembre] de mil ochocientos noventa' - so a place filter will not separate the two towns, and this archive should stop assuming it does. (2) THE TRINIDAD SWEEP MISSED THE SERENA SPELLING: one volume pair of 1905-09 alone carries SARA SERENA, PIO C. SERENA (also written PERENA), ALEJANDRO SERENA and ALBA LERENA, none of them in a town this archive has swept twice. (3) A THIRD AND FOURTH CHILD for Fernando Moratorio and Josefa Lerena Traibel - MARIA DOLORES and FERNANDO - with the grandparents named on both sides, AVELINO and AMBROSIA TRAIBEL among them. BUT THE VOLUME'S LABEL CANNOT BE TRUSTED FOR A DATE: it is catalogued September 1917 to September 1918 and its own year metadata runs 1871, 1874, 1888, 1918, and Josefa born 1851 cannot bear children in 1917. RECORDED AS A TENSION. Nine people entered, ALL INDEX-LEVEL, NO PLATE OPENED - which after this morning's four collapsed couples is said louder than usual.

src: FamilySearch RECORD INDEX - exact-surname sweep: SERENA with a FLORES, URUGUAY place preference (290 returned, ~22 actually of Flores; all read)
what: Acting on this morning's finding that the Trinidad sweep was run on LERENA and missed SERENA entirely.
pages: all Flores records in the set; pages 1-3 of 290 walked
note: THE SPELLING GAP IS REAL AND IT IS LARGE. SERENA with a Flores place filter returns 290 records where the LERENA sweeps returned none of them. The first hundred alone give CHILDREN OF HOUSEHOLDS THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HOLDS AND HAD NO CHILDREN FOR: two for CUSTODIO LERENA and EMA CARDOZO - the couple of the 1911 double-first-cousin dispensation, whose knot this archive spent weeks on and whose children it had never found - and two for JUAN BERNARDO LERENA PELAEZ and EDUVIGES PELAEZ, the couple of the 1894 dispensation. It also returns KNOWN EVENTS under the other spelling, which is the control: Cipriano's marriage of 6 March 1875 naming MAURICIO SERENA and CASIMIRA MONTANO, Alejandro the younger's of 24 December 1854 naming ALEJANDRO SERENA and MARGARITA FERNANDEZ, and the 1894 intended marriage of Juan and Eduviges. A FOURTH SPELLING APPEARS: 'SEREÑA' with a tilde, beside Lerena, Serena and Perena, all at Trinidad. TWENTY-ONE PEOPLE ENTERED, ALL INDEX-LEVEL. Two of them carry a birth date LATER than their own christening, which is the index and not the register. AND THE COUNT IN THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS ROW WAS WRONG. It said 290 records with 190 unread. q.anyPlace RANKS AND DOES NOT FILTER: page one held 22 Flores records, pages two and three held NONE between them. The Flores seam is about twenty-two records and they are all read; the other 268 are Serenas of other departments, an ordinary Italian surname in Uruguay. The FINDINGS are unaffected - every one of them was on page one.

src: FamilySearch RECORD INDEX - exact-surname sweeps of Flores, Uruguay: PERENA (123), GERENA (66), SEREÑA (290) and LLERENA (110)
what: Finishing the spelling sweep of Trinidad after SERENA proved the LERENA sweeps had missed a whole variant.
pages: every Flores record in each set; paged to where the matches stop
note: FOUR SPELLINGS SWEPT, AND EACH HELD PEOPLE THE OTHERS DID NOT. PERENA: 3 Flores records, giving AMABELIA (1880-1899), a fourth child for Cipriano Lerena and Lauriana Beloqui, and ANTONINO (b.1891) for Doroteo Lerena and Isidora Cardozo. GERENA: 7, giving CASTO LINDOLFO (b.1882), a fifth child for Cipriano; VENANCIO, married at Trinidad on 24 April 1885 and THE FIRST CHILD THIS ARCHIVE HAS FOUND OF EITHER MARRIAGE OF ALEJANDRO LERENA THE YOUNGER; and JUAN PEDRO (b.1909), a second child for Buenaventura Olivera and Luisa Lerena whose brother came from the SERENA sweep an hour earlier - ONE HOUSEHOLD, TWO SPELLINGS, TWO SWEEPS. LLERENA: 11, completing the household of FERMIN LERENA and PAULINA BARRAGAN with ISABEL (m. Juan Rodriguez 1902) and a younger FERMIN (m.1924), giving FAUSTINO a wife (VITERBA DE ARRASCAETA), a son (PEDRO, born and dead 1911) and a death (1 June 1914) - and giving BERNABE AND CASIMIRA TWO DAUGHTERS ELEVEN YEARS EARLIER THAN ANYTHING HELD HERE: MARGARITA MEDARDA, christened 1859, a year after their marriage expediente of 15 February 1858, and MARIA, born 13 May 1866. SERENA WITH A TILDE IS NOT A SEPARATE SEAM: 'Sereña' returns the identical 290 records as 'Serena', so FamilySearch normalises the ñ and no tilde variant needs its own sweep. EVERY SET WAS PAGED TO WHERE THE MATCHES STOP, which is the correction this archive made to itself an hour before. Fifteen people entered, all index-level.

src: FamilySearch record index - parent-pair query, 121 cells (13 spellings of the surname as father x as mother), both surnames exact, worldwide, no place or date filter

note: SIZED, THEN RESIZED DOWNWARDS THE SAME DAY.
